name: model-viewer
title: Model Viewer
description: A 3D model (glTF or GLB) in a stage that turns with drag, wheel, pinch and keys, with views, zoom, reset, animation clips and morph weights. The three.js scene (react-three-fiber) is a separate chunk, loaded when the stage nears the viewport and only with WebGL; a poster stands in until then and without WebGL. Agents get rotate, zoom, reset, setView, play, pause and selectClip.

files.content:
import type { ModelViewerView } from "@/components/ui/model-viewer-math"

type ModelViewerLabels = {
  controls: string
  views: string
  view: Record<ModelViewerView, string>
  zoomIn: string
  zoomOut: string
  reset: string
  play: string
  clip: string
  /** Read after the stage's name while it has focus. */
  keyboard: string
  unsupported: string
  error: string
}

const modelViewerLabels: ModelViewerLabels = {
  controls: "3D view controls",
  views: "View",
  view: { front: "Front", "three-quarter": "¾", side: "Side", back: "Back" },
  zoomIn: "Zoom in",
  zoomOut: "Zoom out",
  reset: "Reset view",
  play: "Play animation",
  clip: "Animation",
  keyboard: "Drag or use the arrow keys to turn, + and - to zoom, Home to reset.",
  unsupported: "3D isn't available in this browser.",
  error: "The 3D model could not be loaded.",
}

export { modelViewerLabels }
export type { ModelViewerLabels }

docs: `<ModelViewer model alt poster summary aspectRatio view defaultView onViewChange framing clip defaultClip onClipChange playing defaultPlaying onPlayingChange loop speed weights material background autoRotate controls load overlay sceneChildren onLoad onError error labels>`: `model` is a URL, its bytes (an ArrayBuffer) or a loaded scene (`{ scene, animations }`). The stage is `role="img"` named by `alt`, described by the keyboard hint and the visible `summary`; while it has focus, arrows turn the model, + and - zoom and Home resets. Views are `front`, `three-quarter`, `side` and `back`; free rotation sets the view to `null`. `framing` is `"full"` or a sphere of the model (`{ center: [x, y, z], radius }` in its own units), like a face for a close-up. `weights` are morph target weights by name, from 0 to 1, eased inside the render loop: new weights render React once, never per frame. `playing` left out (or `null`) plays the clip once loaded, except under reduced motion, which also drops auto-rotation and turns every camera move into a jump. `material="toon"` swaps in a three-tone toon material. The canvas draws on demand (`frameloop="demand"`), only while the camera, a clip or a weight moves, and not at all while the stage is out of view or the tab is hidden. Without WebGL, or when loading fails (`labels.error`, announced at once), the poster stays with a message. `preloadModelViewer()` starts loading the scene chunk early; `sceneChildren` puts three.js content of your own inside the canvas, where `ModelViewerSceneContext` gives the viewer's handle and the model's rig. Agent calls before the model has loaded, or for a clip it doesn't have, throw with the reason.
